findings.title: Patch path validation misses invalid `~` escapes after the first token
findings.why: `tokens()` validates a pointer by calling `resolvePointer(null, pointer)` and ignoring everything except a syntax error. `resolvePointer` unescapes the first token, then throws a resolve error because the current value is `null`. It never reaches later tokens. A path such as `/a/~2` or `/a~` followed by more tokens, as in `/a/b~x`, therefore passes. Line 125 then decodes it leniently, so `~2` stays literal. The result is that `applyPatch` reports no `JsonPatchInvalidError`, which the README promises for an invalid `path` or `from`. It may also apply the operation to a member literally named `b~x`. Only an invalid escape in the first token is caught.

findings.title: Token unescaping is duplicated
findings.why: `tokens()` repeats the `~1`/`~0` replace chain that `unescapeToken` already implements. The two copies can drift apart. This is also why the validation gap above exists.

findings.title: Pointless wrapper object `o` in applyOperation
findings.why: `const o = { value: opValue }` is built only to read `o["value"]` back. The destructured `value` could be used directly, which would also remove the `opValue` rename.
